allergyInfo.citrusAllergy: Citrus allergy is rare but documented. Symptoms can include oral allergy syndrome (itching lips/throat) or contact dermatitis from citrus peel oils (limonene).
allergyInfo.crossReactivity: May cross-react with grass pollen or other citrus species.
allergyInfo.sensitivityAdvice: People with gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) may experience acid irritation.

healthInfo.benefits: Rich in ascorbic acid (Vitamin C) supporting immune function and collagen synthesis. High hesperidin flavonoid content contributes to cardiovascular health.
healthInfo.storageRecommendation: Store at cool room temperature for up to 1 week, or refrigerate for 2-3 weeks.
healthInfo.culinaryUses: Fresh snacking, juicing, zest in baking, marmalades.

allergyInfo.citrusAllergy: Possible contact dermatitis from rind terpene compounds (pinene, limonene). Hypersensitivity reactions are uncommon.
allergyInfo.crossReactivity: Occasional cross-reactivity with birch pollen or other Rutaceae species.
allergyInfo.sensitivityAdvice: Slightly less acidic than oranges; usually better tolerated by mild acid-sensitive individuals.

healthInfo.benefits: Contains beta-cryptoxanthin and nobiletin flavonoids which show anti-inflammatory properties and cellular support.
healthInfo.storageRecommendation: Keep in a cool, ventilated container away from direct sunlight for up to 5 days, or refrigerate up to 2 weeks.
healthInfo.culinaryUses: Easy-to-peel fresh snack, salads, candied peel, Asian glazes.

allergyInfo.citrusAllergy: Contact allergy to peel oil (citral, limonene) may cause cheilitis or eczema on hands.
allergyInfo.crossReactivity: Possible cross-reactivity across other members of the genus Citrus.
allergyInfo.sensitivityAdvice: High citric acid content can erode dental enamel if consumed undiluted regularly. May aggravate acid reflux.

healthInfo.benefits: Citrate in lemon juice helps prevent calcium kidney stones by increasing urine volume and pH. High antioxidant profile.
healthInfo.storageRecommendation: Store in the crisper drawer of your refrigerator for up to 3 to 4 weeks.
healthInfo.culinaryUses: Salad dressings, marinades, curds, lemonade, seafood seasoning.

allergyInfo.citrusAllergy: Known risk of phytophotodermatitis: furocoumarins (psoralens) in lime juice/rind react with UV sunlight causing skin blistering and hyperpigmentation (often called 'Margarita burn').
allergyInfo.crossReactivity: Other citrus fruits and Apiaceae plants (celery, parsley).
allergyInfo.sensitivityAdvice: Wash skin thoroughly with soap and water after handling limes before sun exposure.

healthInfo.benefits: High soluble fiber (pectin) and citric acid aiding iron absorption and digestive enzymatic activity.
healthInfo.storageRecommendation: Store in a breathable bag in the refrigerator for up to 3 weeks.
healthInfo.culinaryUses: Ceviche, guacamole, cocktails, Thai and Mexican cuisine, marinades.

allergyInfo.citrusAllergy: Contains high concentrations of citronellal and terpenes in leaves and bumpy rind. May trigger contact allergy in sensitive skin.
allergyInfo.sensitivityAdvice: Rind and leaves are intensely fragrant and bitter; flesh is rarely eaten raw due to very low juice and extreme astringency.

healthInfo.benefits: Essential oils from leaves show strong antimicrobial, antioxidant, and insect-repellent properties in botanical studies.
healthInfo.storageRecommendation: Leaves freeze exceptionally well for up to 1 year. Fruit keeps in refrigerator for 2-3 weeks.
healthInfo.culinaryUses: Double leaves torn and infused in Tom Yum soup, green curries, and Southeast Asian pastes.
